newsitem.title: CANADA: Investors keep cheering CanOxy takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: Investors keep cheering CanOxy takeover bid.

text.p: Investors continued on Friday to scoop up shares of Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd in the wake of its C$2-billion white knight bid for Wascana Energy Inc as excitement grew about potential benefits from the deal.
CanOxy was trading up 1.00 to 26.95 on 1.8 million shares late in Friday's Toronto Stock Exchange session.
The stock, which has climbed from 23.50 on Monday, the day before it announced its C$20.50 cash per share bid for Wascana, had jumped as high as 27.10 in Friday trade.

Bill Magee, analyst with Credifinance Securities in Toronto, said CanOxy was expected to reap rewards from both increased cash flow and a higher cash flow multiple if it is successful in its bid for Regina-based Wascana.
It is still not clear whether Talisman Energy Inc, whose original cash-and-stock offer for Wascana expires on Monday, will extend its bid and attempt to glean more value from the company's assets.
"Should CanOxy succeed here, it's quite a coup and my...analysis suggests the multiple should improve," Magee said.
He said the market tended to afford Canadian oil companies multiples of six times cash flow or higher for domestic operations and four times for international.
CanOxy's international operations pumped out about 69 percent of its cash flow before the deal, he said.
"They will become 50 percent international and 50 percent domestic (if the deal was successful)," Magee said. "
"So, the multiple just by simple arithmatic should go from 4.2 to 4.7 (times). We apply that to the pro forma cash flow that they're forecasting this year and you end up with a C$32 target price."

He also said the bid showed investors uncertainty regarding the company's management that arose after Bernard Isautier resigned as CanOxy chief executive in late 1995 was unfounded. The company's current chief is David Hentschel.
"The new gentleman has definitely proven that he's a shooter and prepared to do big things. I think this will help the general psychology surrounding the company."
